'''''Lagarosiphon major''''' is a [[Monocotyledon|monocotic]] [[aquatic plant]] native to [[Southern Africa]]. Common names include '''African elodea''', '''curly waterweed''', '''oxygen weed''' and '''South African oxygen weed'''. It is used as freshwater aquarium plant.

It is an [[invasive species|invasive plant]] in some countries.<ref>[http://www.issg.org/database/species/ecology.asp?si=403&fr=1&sts=sss&lang=EN Global Invasive Species Database] - ''Lagarosiphon major'' entry</ref> In [[New Zealand]] it is listed on the [[National Pest Plant Accord]], and it is classed as a noxious weed in the [[United States]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=LAMA15|title=Plants Profile for Lagarosiphon major (oxygen-weed)|website=plants.usda.gov|access-date=2017-01-31}}</ref> ''Lagarosiphon major'' was added to the [[European Union]]'s 
[[List of invasive alien species of Union concern|List of Invasive Alien Species of Union concern]] on 3 August 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|title=List of Invasive Alien Species of Union concern - Environment - European Commission |url=https://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/invasivealien/list/index_en.htm |access-date=2021-06-04|website=ec.europa.eu}}</ref> meaning that – amongst other things – it is illegal to sell it anywhere in the European Union or to dump it in the environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Europese IUS Verordening|url=https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/NL/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R1143&from=EN}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Ireland: Co.Galway in parts of upper Lough Corrib.<ref>Pybus, C. and O'Halloran, P. 2009. Distribution of some submerged aquatic macrophytes in the Eglinton Canal. ''Ir. Nat. J.''  '''30''': 51-53.</ref>
